# Reconstructing a withheld museum catalogue declaration

Can an archive detect inconsistent or missing declarations by comparing sibling records within an accession? The outcome is the current Metropolitan Museum of Art CSV's literal Is Public Domain flag. A forecast serves retrospective metadata QA only. The archive itself publishes conditions for reuse. This is a distinct predictive follow-up to the Cleveland and Chicago proxy audit. [Met collection data and terms](https://github.com/metmuseum/openaccess/tree/15d35b4b1f7f87baa8d42cc24481f68f76817d20) · [Met image use](https://www.metmuseum.org/about-the-met/policies-and-documents/image-resources)

Use a fixed digest of Object ID for an artificial item-level missingness experiment. Training buckets 0–59, development 60–79, reserve 80–99 without reading their flags. Exclude rights strings, media locations, third-party flags, gallery assignment, editorial highlight and timeline flags. Use object begin/end dates, recorded accession year, department, classification, object name, first constituent ID and accession family (object number with its last dot-delimited segment removed). A single-segment number has no inferred family. Include a matched simple predictor that uses the observed training family rate, an ordered-target-statistic CatBoost model with the same categories and numerical metadata, and a model supplementing these with regularized training-only family and artist frequencies. The candidate adds training-label information for nearby sibling IDs within the same accession family and within artist, and the artist–family conjunction. Fit the learned neighborhood features out of fold in training. Development can query only the training label store. Empty keys never pool unrelated objects. Output pooled log loss, plus seen-family and unseen-family strata. The screen is .005 nats improvement over every control. Compare matched predictors and audit what is already predictable from catalogue structure before allocating the untouched split. The development data are available for method refinement. A publication claim also needs documented source-label semantics, relevant published imputation methods, an independent collection and an eval regime reflecting an actual missingness mechanism.
